title: Let All the World Abroad
description: Let All the World Abroad in Tonic Solfa to QUAM DILECTA, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sixes (6.6.6.6), and this page sets them to QUAM DILECTA; any other Sixes tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let all the world a-broad In cheer-ful praise u-nite To bless the name of God, Cre-a-tor, Lord of might.

lines: To bless the name of God,
He made the sea and land,
The heavens that, day and night,
The sun and moon, whose light
First called his soul to live.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to QUAM DILECTA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
